segments.futureReducer: Implement and validate the proposed contract resolver and family-owned execution path once, then measure whether Batch 2 targets inherit it with zero target-ID production wiring.

segments.cause: The Founder handoff must prove that the proposed scale architecture is complete, measured, and has not changed runtime or locked governance.
segments.futureReducer: A specification lint can automate required-section, architecture-diff, file-scope, and ledger-reconciliation checks.

segments.futureReducer: The contract resolver and family registry make future work governed data and authority packaging when a compatible executor already exists.

segments.futureReducer: A new approved product can now inherit the generic page, family SEC, preservation, catalog, and asset build through its contract package.

segments.workPerformed: Official experiment clock anchor to the first recorded active target-processing segment.
segments.cause: Founder anchored the official experiment at 8:46 PM EDT; the first active segment began eight seconds later.
segments.futureReducer: Automatic ledger start can eliminate this unclassified transition.

segments.workPerformed: Loaded Founder approval, confirmed the active Episode 56 and KTIS authority, inspected the existing target registry and authority-package patterns, and established the governed experiment records.
segments.cause: The approved cohort required an explicit governed identity boundary, provenance record, and contemporaneous measurement foundation before target registration could begin.
segments.futureReducer: A reusable cohort-intake manifest and ledger initializer could generate these records from a Founder-approved cohort while preserving the first-pass baseline.

segments.workPerformed: Inspected all 12 official GunFun product pages and publisher-hosted target representations; captured original or highest-observed assets; recorded dimensions, hashes, visible printed instructions, scoring, and rules; and separated absent authority from authority printed on the target itself.
segments.cause: Product-page text alone omitted material authority printed on several targets, so the publisher representations had to be inspected before gaps could be classified correctly.
segments.futureReducer: Publisher Authority Profiles should ingest and hash the publisher product representation alongside commerce metadata, then surface printed-authority review as a standard intake step.

segments.workPerformed: Packaged source URLs, local evidence paths, SHA-256 hashes, pixel dimensions, visible printed authority, UGO fitness, claim boundaries, and remaining gaps into one cohort publisher-authority audit.
segments.cause: Raw publisher evidence must be converted into a stable, reviewable authority boundary before registration can safely consume it.
segments.futureReducer: A declarative Publisher Authority Profile importer could generate the repeated identity, representation, hash, and source-audit fields while leaving human review for claims and gaps.

segments.workPerformed: Created 12 declarative target-knowledge manifests preserving E56 identity, publisher SKU, target type, cautious mission routing, evidence model, known geometry, source audit, and explicit unknowns. Execution remained unavailable by default.
segments.cause: Each known publisher SKU needs a distinct governed registry identity even when runtime authority is incomplete.
segments.futureReducer: Publisher Authority Profile data should emit target-knowledge manifests directly; target-specific human work should remain only for mission semantics and exception review.

segments.workPerformed: Validated all JSON artifacts, checked whitespace integrity, loaded the live registry, proved 12 unique GunFun SKUs are recognized, and proved none were accidentally execution-authorized.
segments.cause: Registration must prove both positive recognition and fail-closed execution behavior.
segments.futureReducer: A standard cohort contract test can automatically assert cohort cardinality, SKU uniqueness, authority gaps, and fail-closed defaults.

segments.workPerformed: Traced registered manifests through target_registry, mission_registry, session_authority, and the inherited catalog authority engine. Normalized proposed routing to existing mission/result families and identified the shared execution-admission boundary.
segments.cause: The target registry loads new JSON manifests but forces them to unavailable; support can only be granted by Python override dictionaries and hard-coded target allowlists. Session authority and catalog execution routing are also target-ID keyed in application code.
segments.futureReducer: Move governed lifecycle/support declarations, mission routing, session admission, UGO classifier selection, and result-package dispatch into validated registry data consumed by existing shared owners. Preserve fail-closed validation and Founder approval state.

segments.workPerformed: Normalized target routing to existing mission/result families, packaged Pass 001 findings, revalidated registry recognition and fail-closed execution, verified representation hashes, and prepared the Founder decision-boundary report.
segments.cause: The first-pass handoff required an internally consistent classification and measured record after the shared platform boundary was found.
segments.futureReducer: A cohort closeout validator can calculate metrics and produce the first-pass status report directly from validated manifests and ledger segments.

segments.workPerformed: Applied the final first-pass classification to every target, distinguished data-only knowledge registration from end-to-end runtime registration, normalized E56-T10 to the existing smartEvidenceCapture family without importing numeric scoring, and packaged machine-readable and human-readable cohort results.
segments.cause: The governed first pass requires one mutually exclusive outcome for each target and must not confuse knowledge recognition with executable support.
segments.futureReducer: A cohort classifier can derive outcomes from authority-gap state, UGO readiness, and execution-registration capability once those fields are declarative.

segments.workPerformed: Ran final cohort cardinality, classification-count, registry-recognition, fail-closed execution, mission/result-family, ledger-allocation, JSON, and diff-integrity checks; calculated elapsed and active-work summaries.
segments.cause: The final result must prove population count, outcome count, fail-closed behavior, timing reconciliation, and artifact integrity before handoff.
segments.futureReducer: A single cohort-closeout command can run and record these validations automatically.

segments.workPerformed: Attempted the established computer-vision geometry inspection path, found OpenCV unavailable in both system and bundled runtimes, and established the available Pillow/numpy fallback without downloading or installing dependencies.

segments.futureReducer: A declared, preflighted geometry-analysis runtime would eliminate dependency discovery during target work.

segments.workPerformed: Derived publisher-grounded target-plane landmarks and zone observations, packaged six data-only UGO registration candidates, linked them from target manifests, and preserved independent trace and empirical runtime-gate requirements. segments.futureReducer: A publisher-asset geometry extractor plus an independent UGO review workflow could generate landmarks, carry source hashes, and flag unresolved boundaries automatically.
